Root cause found. Not backend mixing in config — both sides git-refs. It's a **push gap**: checkpoint ref born on another machine, never reached checkpoint remote.

## What happened

**Backend routing correct, no mix.**
- `.entire/settings.json` → `checkpoints.primary.type: git-refs`. Consistent.
- `01KYSGR4W1ZATZRW47J510EZGJ` = ULID → read router sends ULIDs to **git-refs** backend (hex IDs would go to the v1 branch). Right call.

**The ref just doesn't exist anywhere you can reach:**

| Location | ref `.../GJ/01KYSGR4W1ZATZRW47J510EZGJ` |
|---|---|
| local `refs/entire/**` (98 refs) | ❌ absent |
| remote `cli-checkpoints.git` (379 refs) | ❌ absent |

`git ls-remote` for it → exit 0, empty. CLI does `git fetch <that ref>` → git exits **128** ("couldn't find remote ref") → code maps best-effort fetch failure to **"checkpoint not found"**. That's the whole chain.

**Where the ID came from:** commit `4e229c0546` (HEAD of `feat/repo-mirror-use`, author **Matthias Wenz**) carries trailer `Entire-Checkpoint: 01KYSGR4W1ZATZRW47J510EZGJ`. Not your checkpoint — made on another machine / cloud trail runner.

## Why ref missing

git-refs backend (`refs_store.go:150-175`): checkpoint write does two things —
1. `SetReference` local ref (instant)
2. `enqueueForPush` → push-discovery queue, drained **best-effort at pre-push**

The **branch commit reached origin** (feat branch pushed → trailer visible to you). But the **per-checkpoint ref never reached `cli-checkpoints.git`**. On the creating machine the pre-push queue drain didn't fire or failed silently (best-effort, logs Warn, never blocks). Two decoupled pushes: branch → origin ✓, checkpoint ref → checkpoint remote ✗.

So "mixing backends?" No. "branch vs git-refs?" Routing right — data orphaned. Commit trailer points at a git-refs checkpoint that exists only on the author's local machine.

## Fix / recover

Nothing you can do locally — data not on any remote. Options:
- **Owner re-pushes**: on Matthias's machine (or the trail's cloud worktree) the ref still exists locally. Push it: `git push https://github.com/entireio/cli-checkpoints.git refs/entire/checkpoints/GJ/01KYSGR4W1ZATZRW47J510EZGJ`, or `entire hooks git pre-push` there to drain the queue.
- **Resume itself still worked** — branch switched, checkpoint fine. Only the AI session transcript restore is unavailable.

Real bug worth filing: cloud trail runner should push checkpoint refs (drain the discovery queue) before the worktree dies, else every cloud-built trail resumes with dangling checkpoints. Best-effort silent-Warn push means the failure is invisible until someone resumes.

- Commit trailers are defined in `cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go`. ## 1. Trail linkage (commit/checkpoint → trail number/URL)

**There is no local mapping.** A trail is resolved from a **branch name** via the control-plane API. So the chain is: commit → branch → trail (network call required).

Getting the branch for your commit (all local, git-native):
- `session.State.Branch` — the branch HEAD pointed at when the session last took a turn (`cmd/entire/cli/session/state.go:136-142`). This is the intended "map a stopped session back to its branch" field.

- `findTrailByBranch(ctx, client, forge, owner, repo, branch)` at `trail_cmd.go:1899` — matches `t.Branch == branch`.
- `findTrailBySelector` at `trail_cmd.go:1875` — accepts a trail number, id, or branch string.
- `findTrailByNumber` at `trail_cmd.go:1906`.

The resulting `api.TrailResource` (`cmd/entire/cli/api/trail_types.go:22-53`) gives you the trail Number, URL, Title, Status, Base, etc.

Trail number → URL:
- Prefer `TrailResource.URL` (server-supplied).
- Fallback constructor `trailWebURL(base, forge, owner, repo, number)` at `trail_cmd.go:369` → `<origin>/<forge>/<owner>/<repo>/trails/<number>`.
- `trailDisplayURL` at `trail_cmd.go:353` encapsulates the prefer-URL-else-build logic.

Repo/forge resolution: `resolveTrailRemote(ctx)` at `trail_cmd.go:1990` → `gitremote.ResolveRemoteRepo(ctx, "origin")` returns `(forge, owner, repo)`.

Trail metadata display struct: `trail.Metadata` at `cmd/entire/cli/trail/trail.go:134-153` (Number, TrailID, URL, Branch, Base, Title, Body, Status, Phase, Author, Assignees, Labels, Type, Priority, Reviewers, CreatedAt, UpdatedAt, MergedAt). Client: `api.Client` in `cmd/entire/cli/api/client.go` (methods `Get/Post/Patch/Delete` at :135-177; `DecodeJSON`). Base URL via `api.BaseURL()`.

Trail endpoints (all require network + auth):

# Plan: Daily checkpoint-availability audit job

## Context

We hit a real failure: `entire trail resume 955` could not restore its session because
checkpoint `01KYSGR4W1ZATZRW47J510EZGJ` (trailer `Entire-Checkpoint:` on commit `4e229c05`,
branch `feat/repo-mirror-use`, author Matthias Wenz) exists in the commit trailer and on
`origin`, but its git-refs checkpoint ref `refs/entire/checkpoints/GJ/01KYSGR4W1...EZGJ` was
**never pushed** to the checkpoint remote `github.com/entireio/cli-checkpoints`. The git-refs
backend enqueues checkpoint refs for a best-effort pre-push drain (`enqueueForPush`,
`cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/refs_store.go:164`); when that drain never runs or fails silently,
the branch commit reaches origin while the checkpoint ref is orphaned on the creating machine.
The failure is invisible until someone tries to resume.

**Goal:** an active, scheduled (daily) audit that walks every commit created in the last 24h
across all branches, extracts each `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer, checks whether the matching ref
exists on the checkpoint remote, and — if any are missing — **fails the job** and emits a report
table (with per-commit context) to the GitHub run summary, an uploaded artifact, and Slack.

## Decisions (confirmed with user)

- **Commit scope:** all branches (`git log --branches --remotes --since=...`).
- **Engine:** a CI **shell script** (`scripts/checkpoint-audit.sh`) — no new Go/CLI surface.
- **Context per missing checkpoint:** commit-native only (no control-plane/trail API, no
  `ENTIRE_TOKEN`): checkpoint ID, commit short SHA, author, containing branch(es), date, subject.
- **Reporting:** fail the job + `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` table + uploaded artifact + Slack message.

## Design

Robustness without Go comes from leaning on git's native primitives instead of hand-rolled
regex/shard math:
- **Trailer extraction:** `git show -s --format='%(trailers:key=Entire-Checkpoint,valueonly=true)'`
  — git parses the trailer itself and returns one ID per line, handling squash-merge commits that
  carry multiple `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers.
- **Remote set:** one `git ls-remote <checkpoint-url> 'refs/entire/checkpoints/*'`; the checkpoint
  ID is the ref **leaf** (`refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<ID>` → `<ID>`), so membership is a plain
  string-set lookup — no shard arithmetic, works for both legacy-hex and ULID IDs.
- **Auth:** RFC 7617 basic header, matching the CLI (`CheckpointTokenEnvVar`,
  `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/remote/git.go:34`). Avoid creds-in-URL:
  `git -c http.extraheader="AUTHORIZATION: basic $(printf 'x-access-token:%s' "$TOKEN" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" ls-remote https://github.com/<repo>.git ...`.

### New file: `scripts/checkpoint-audit.sh`

`#!/usr/bin/env bash`, `set -euo pipefail`. Mirrors the tri-state exit convention of
`scripts/create-nightly-tag.sh` (0 = ok, non-zero = drift/error).

Inputs (env, with defaults):
- `CHECKPOINT_REPO` (default `entireio/cli-checkpoints`)
- `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN` (required to reach a private checkpoint repo)
- `AUDIT_WINDOW` (default `24 hours ago`)
- `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, `AUDIT_REPORT_FILE` (default `checkpoint-audit-report.md`) — optional sinks.

Logic:
1. Build the remote checkpoint-ID set via `ls-remote` (extraheader auth); `awk` the ref leaf into
   a sorted, deduped lookup (assoc array or `grep -Fxq` against a temp file). Fail fast (exit 2) if
   `ls-remote` errors — a broken remote must not read as "0 missing".
2. `git log --branches --remotes --since="$AUDIT_WINDOW" --format='%H'` → candidate SHAs.
3. Per SHA: read `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer value(s). For each ID not in the remote set, collect
   context in one `git show -s --format='%h%x1f%an%x1f%aI%x1f%s'` plus containing branches from
   `git branch -a --contains "$SHA" --format='%(refname:short)'` (filter to `origin/*`, strip prefix,
   dedupe). Append a report row.
4. Emit a markdown table (`Checkpoint | Commit | Author | Branch(es) | Date | Subject`) plus a summary
   line (`scanned N commits, M checkpoints, K missing`) to stdout, to `$AUDIT_REPORT_FILE`, and — if
   set — to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`. Also write a machine-readable `checkpoint-audit-report.json`
   (array of missing entries) for the artifact.
5. Exit `1` when `K > 0`, `0` otherwise (`2` reserved for remote/setup errors).

Because we already know `01KYSGR4W1ZATZRW47J510EZGJ` is genuinely missing, a wide-window local run
is a built-in end-to-end fixture (see Verification).

### New file: `.github/workflows/checkpoint-audit.yml`

Modeled on `nightly.yml` (cron + App-token skeleton, SHA-pinned actions, `workflow_dispatch`
alongside `schedule`) with reporting borrowed from `e2e.yml`'s `notify-slack` job.

```yaml
name: Checkpoint Audit
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 7 * * *"      # daily 07:00 UTC (GitHub does not honor sub-daily cron reliably)
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      window: { description: "git --since window", default: "24 hours ago" }
permissions:
  contents: read
concurrency:
  group: checkpoint-audit-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```

Steps:
1. `actions/create-github-app-token@<sha>` scoped to `owner: entireio`,
   `repositories: cli-checkpoints` → the token for `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN`.
   **Prereq:** the App must be installed on `entireio/cli-checkpoints` with Contents:read. If the
   existing `HOMEBREW_TAP_APP_*` App is not installed there, add a new App secret pair (e.g.
   `CHECKPOINT_AUDIT_APP_ID` / `CHECKPOINT_AUDIT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`) or a read-only PAT secret.
2. `actions/checkout@<sha>` with `fetch-depth: 0`.
3. `git fetch --all --prune` so `--branches --remotes` sees every branch (checkout only brings the
   default branch history).
4. Run audit step (`id: audit`, `continue-on-error: true` so downstream reporting always runs):
   `scripts/checkpoint-audit.sh`, env `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN`, `AUDIT_WINDOW`, `CHECKPOINT_REPO`.
5. `actions/upload-artifact@<sha>` (`if: always()`, `retention-days: 7`) for the `.md` + `.json`.
6. Slack notify (`if: always() && steps.audit.outcome == 'failure'`): `slackapi/slack-github-action@<sha>`,
   `webhook: ${{ secrets.E2E_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL }}`, Block Kit payload with the summary line, the
   (truncated) table, and a link to the run.
7. Gate step (`if: steps.audit.outcome == 'failure'`): `exit 1` — makes the job red after reporting.

### Optional: local task

Add `[tasks."checkpoint:audit"]` to `mise.toml` that runs `scripts/checkpoint-audit.sh`, so
engineers can audit locally (`ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN=… mise run checkpoint:audit`).

## Files

- **New** `scripts/checkpoint-audit.sh` — the audit engine (git-native trailer + ls-remote diff).
- **New** `.github/workflows/checkpoint-audit.yml` — daily scheduled job + Slack/artifact reporting.
- **Edit** `mise.toml` — add `checkpoint:audit` task (optional local runner).

## Reused primitives / references

- Ref layout `refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>` — `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/refs_naming.go:19`.
- Checkpoint token auth (RFC 7617) — `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/remote/git.go:34` (`ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN`).
- CI templates — `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` (cron + App token), `.github/workflows/e2e.yml`
  (`notify-slack`, artifact upload), `scripts/create-nightly-tag.sh` (tri-state exit).
- Checkpoint remote configured in `.entire/settings.json` → `entireio/cli-checkpoints`.

## Verification

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Audit checkpoint availability on the checkpoint remote.
#
# Walks every commit created within a time window across all branches, extracts
# each `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer, and checks whether the matching checkpoint
# ref exists on the checkpoint remote (github.com/<CHECKPOINT_REPO>). Any commit
# whose checkpoint ref is missing from the remote is reported with context and
# makes the script exit non-zero.
#
# This catches the failure mode where a commit reaches origin but its git-refs
# checkpoint ref (refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>) was never pushed to the
# checkpoint remote — the checkpoint is then unrecoverable on any other machine
# (e.g. `entire trail resume` / `entire explain` fail with "checkpoint not found").
#
# Trailer parsing and ref-set membership use git's own primitives rather than
# hand-rolled regex/shard math: `git show --format='%(trailers:...)'` parses
# trailers (handling squash-merge commits with multiple checkpoint trailers), and
# the checkpoint ID is simply the ref leaf, so membership is a plain string-set
# lookup that works for both legacy-hex and ULID IDs.
#
# Env (all optional except the token for a private remote):
#   ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN  GitHub token with read access to the checkpoint repo.
#                            Sent as an RFC 7617 basic auth header (matching the
#                            CLI), so it never appears in a remote URL.
#   CHECKPOINT_REPO          owner/repo of the checkpoint remote
#                            (default: entireio/cli-checkpoints).
#   AUDIT_WINDOW             git `--since` window (default: "24 hours ago").
#   AUDIT_REPORT_FILE        markdown report sink (default: checkpoint-audit-report.md).
#   AUDIT_JSON_FILE          machine-readable report sink (default: checkpoint-audit-report.json).
#   GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY      if set, the markdown report is appended to it.
#
# Exit codes: 0 = all present, 1 = one or more checkpoints missing, 2 = setup or
# remote error (a broken remote must never read as "0 missing").

CHECKPOINT_REPO="${CHECKPOINT_REPO:-entireio/cli-checkpoints}"
AUDIT_WINDOW="${AUDIT_WINDOW:-24 hours ago}"
AUDIT_REPORT_FILE="${AUDIT_REPORT_FILE:-checkpoint-audit-report.md}"
AUDIT_JSON_FILE="${AUDIT_JSON_FILE:-checkpoint-audit-report.json}"
TOKEN="${ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN:-}"

CHECKPOINT_URL="https://github.com/${CHECKPOINT_REPO}.git"

REMOTE_IDS_FILE=$(mktemp)
ROWS_FILE=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$REMOTE_IDS_FILE" "$ROWS_FILE"' EXIT

# json_str emits a JSON string literal, escaping backslashes and double quotes.
# Author names and subjects are single-line, so control-char escaping is not needed.
json_str() {
  local s=${1//\\/\\\\}
  s=${s//\"/\\\"}
  printf '"%s"' "$s"
}

# 1. Enumerate the checkpoint refs present on the remote (names only, no object
#    transfer). The ID is the ref leaf: refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<ID>.
echo "Enumerating checkpoint refs on ${CHECKPOINT_REPO} ..." >&2
if [ -n "$TOKEN" ]; then
  auth_b64=$(printf 'x-access-token:%s' "$TOKEN" | base64 | tr -d '\n')
  remote_refs=$(git -c "http.extraheader=AUTHORIZATION: basic ${auth_b64}" \
    ls-remote "$CHECKPOINT_URL" 'refs/entire/checkpoints/*') || {
    echo "::error::failed to ls-remote ${CHECKPOINT_REPO} (check ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN and repo access)" >&2
    exit 2
  }
else
  remote_refs=$(git ls-remote "$CHECKPOINT_URL" 'refs/entire/checkpoints/*') || {
    echo "::error::failed to ls-remote ${CHECKPOINT_REPO} (no ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN set; is the repo private?)" >&2
    exit 2
  }
fi

printf '%s\n' "$remote_refs" \
  | awk '$2 ~ /^refs\/entire\/checkpoints\// { id = $2; sub(/.*\//, "", id); print id }' \
  | sort -u > "$REMOTE_IDS_FILE"
remote_count=$(grep -c . "$REMOTE_IDS_FILE" || true)

# 2. Candidate commits: every branch commit in the window (local heads + remotes),
#    de-duplicated while preserving order.
commits=$(git log --branches --remotes --since="$AUDIT_WINDOW" --format='%H' | awk '!seen[$0]++')

# 3. For each commit, diff its checkpoint trailers against the remote set.
commit_count=0
cp_count=0
missing_count=0
while IFS= read -r sha; do
  [ -z "$sha" ] && continue
  commit_count=$((commit_count + 1))
  cps=$(git show -s --format='%(trailers:key=Entire-Checkpoint,valueonly=true)' "$sha")
  while IFS= read -r cp; do
    cp="${cp//[[:space:]]/}"
    [ -z "$cp" ] && continue
    cp_count=$((cp_count + 1))
    if grep -Fxq "$cp" "$REMOTE_IDS_FILE"; then
      continue
    fi
    missing_count=$((missing_count + 1))
    meta=$(git show -s --format='%h%x1f%an%x1f%aI%x1f%s' "$sha")
    short=${meta%%$'\x1f'*}; meta=${meta#*$'\x1f'}
    author=${meta%%$'\x1f'*}; meta=${meta#*$'\x1f'}
    cdate=${meta%%$'\x1f'*}; subject=${meta#*$'\x1f'}
    branches=$(git branch -a --contains "$sha" --format='%(refname:short)' 2>/dev/null \
      | sed -e 's#^remotes/##' -e 's#^origin/##' \
      | grep -v '^entire/' \
      | awk 'NF && !s[$0]++' \
      | paste -sd', ' -)
    printf '%s\x1e%s\x1e%s\x1e%s\x1e%s\x1e%s\n' \
      "$cp" "$short" "$author" "${branches:-?}" "$cdate" "$subject" >> "$ROWS_FILE"
  done <<EOF
$cps
EOF
done <<EOF
$commits
EOF

# 4. Render the markdown report (stdout + file + optional step summary).
{
  echo "# Checkpoint availability audit"
  echo
  echo "- Window: commits since \`${AUDIT_WINDOW}\`"
  echo "- Checkpoint remote: \`${CHECKPOINT_REPO}\` (${remote_count} refs present)"
  echo "- Scanned: ${commit_count} commit(s), ${cp_count} checkpoint trailer(s)"
  echo "- **Missing from remote: ${missing_count}**"
  echo
  if [ "$missing_count" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "| Checkpoint | Commit | Author | Branch(es) | Date | Subject |"
    echo "|---|---|---|---|---|---|"
    while IFS=$'\x1e' read -r cp short author branches cdate subject; do
      subject=${subject//|/\\|}
      echo "| \`${cp}\` | \`${short}\` | ${author} | ${branches} | ${cdate} | ${subject} |"
    done < "$ROWS_FILE"
  else
    echo "All checkpoints referenced in the window are present on the remote. :white_check_mark:"
  fi
} | tee "$AUDIT_REPORT_FILE"

if [ -n "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-}" ]; then
  cat "$AUDIT_REPORT_FILE" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
fi

# 5. Machine-readable report for the artifact.
{
  echo "["
  first=1
  while IFS=$'\x1e' read -r cp short author branches cdate subject; do
    if [ "$first" -eq 1 ]; then first=0; else echo ","; fi
    printf '  {"checkpoint":%s,"commit":%s,"author":%s,"branches":%s,"date":%s,"subject":%s}' \
      "$(json_str "$cp")" "$(json_str "$short")" "$(json_str "$author")" \
      "$(json_str "$branches")" "$(json_str "$cdate")" "$(json_str "$subject")"
  done < "$ROWS_FILE"
  echo
  echo "]"
} > "$AUDIT_JSON_FILE"

if [ "$missing_count" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "::error::${missing_count} checkpoint(s) missing from ${CHECKPOINT_REPO}" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "All ${cp_count} checkpoint(s) present on ${CHECKPOINT_REPO}." >&2
exit 0

name: Checkpoint Audit

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 7 * * *" # 07:00 UTC daily (GitHub does not honor sub-daily cron reliably)
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      window:
        description: 'git --since window to audit'
        default: '24 hours ago'

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: checkpoint-audit-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  audit:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Generate checkpoint-repo token
        id: app-token
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.HOMEBREW_TAP_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.HOMEBREW_TAP_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          owner: ${{ github.repository_owner }}
          repositories: cli-checkpoints

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Fetch all branches
        run: git fetch --all --prune

      - name: Run checkpoint audit
        id: audit
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          AUDIT_WINDOW: ${{ github.event.inputs.window || '24 hours ago' }}
        run: scripts/checkpoint-audit.sh

      - name: Upload audit report
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7
        with:
          name: checkpoint-audit-report
          path: |
            checkpoint-audit-report.md
            checkpoint-audit-report.json
          retention-days: 7

      - name: Notify Slack of missing checkpoints
        if: ${{ always() && steps.audit.outcome == 'failure' }}
        uses: slackapi/slack-github-action@dcb1066f776dd043e64d0e8ba94ca15cc7e1875d # v4.0.0
        with:
          webhook: ${{ secrets.E2E_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL }}
          webhook-type: incoming-webhook
          payload: |
            {
              "attachments": [
                {
                  "color": "#d50200",
                  "blocks": [
                    {
                      "type": "section",
                      "text": {
                        "type": "mrkdwn",
                        "text": ":red_circle: *Checkpoint audit found missing checkpoints*\n\nOne or more commits reference a checkpoint that is not on the checkpoint remote. See the report artifact for the full table.\n\n<${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}|View run details>"
                      }
                    }
                  ]
                }
              ]
            }

      - name: Fail if checkpoints are missing
        if: ${{ steps.audit.outcome == 'failure' }}
        run: |
          echo "::error::checkpoint audit reported missing checkpoints"
          exit 1

The git-refs backend enqueues checkpoint refs for a best-effort pre-push drain; when that drain never runs or fails silently, the branch commit and the checkpoint ref diverge — and the gap is invisible until someone tries to resume.
